x: Welcome to new members Pat Shepperd, Cliff Calderwood, Peter Sharp, Graham Millard, Peter Colledge, Ian Doick and Martin Bloice.

Cliff Calderwood looked as if he would make the scoring five when John Hamilton faded away but he was outrun by Nigel Bacon and Robert Poole who clinched third place for Belgrave in a close team result.
Backing them up we have Cliff Calderwood, Geoff Rosam, Peter Sharp and Pat Shepherd. This has the makings of a first class team who already have the right spirit.

Bill Curtin was a comfortable winner of this year's Youths' championship over 2½ miles of wet going on a dank Saturday afternoon. He held off Cliff Calderwood with something in hand and both ran faster than John Kelly's winning time of 15:52 last year.

Run in dangerous, icy conditions and a blizzard thrown in at the end for good measure, our lads really rose to the occasion and, led by Cliff Calderwood, split Walton and Mitcham in the team event - leaving us only 11points down at the halfway stage of the competition.
Cliff Calderwood was a non-starter and this almost certainly pushed us out of the medals. Nevertheless our 5th place was two better than last year and Day ran well to lead our team home.
Although not fully recovered from an ankle injury, Cliff Calderwood elected to turn out for our team on this tough course but was unable to get within 100 places of his normal form.
Clifford Owen Calderwood was born at Isleworth, Middlesex on 17.12.49. But for his brother Dick (also a Belgravian) he would not be carrying a claret & gold vest in our Youth teams today.

Cliff Calderwood was still not fully recovered from recent injury and was well over 100 places outside his best form. Our team will benefit greatly from the experience if it has persuaded them to approach their training with even more determination.

Our bright young prospects, Dick Piotrowski and Cliff Calderwood pulled off the Club 10 miles and 5 miles championships respectively and impressed the onlookers with a brand of running that holds a bright future for both.

Tony Brien was favourite to take Cliff Calderwood's title, but few expected the margin to be as great at 1½ minutes. There is little doubt that he would have been up with the leading five in the Senior race had he opted for the '10'.
